record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Given a signed graph Σ and an edge e, determine whether e lies in exactly one negative circle of Σ.

evidence.quote: E3. In Σ, is a certain edge e in a unique negative circle? Ans. Medium hard: It depends on the Tutte 3-decomposition of Γ into 2-connected subgraphs, and how those subgraphs are signed (Behr [1]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair Σ = (Γ, σ) where Γ = (V, E) is a finite graph and σ : E → {+1, −1} is an assignment of signs to its edges. A circle (cycle) C in Γ is called negative if the product of the signs of its edges, ∏_{e ∈ C} σ(e), equals −1, and positive otherwise.

Given a signed graph Σ and a distinguished edge e ∈ E(Γ), give a structural characterization (and an efficient decision procedure) determining whether e is contained in exactly one negative circle of Σ. The characterization should describe both:
(a) the conditions on the underlying graph Γ (e.g., in terms of bridges of circles through e and the decomposition of Γ into 2-connected components / 2-separations), and
(b) the conditions on the signature σ on the resulting pieces,
that are necessary and sufficient for e to lie in a unique negative circle.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was resolved by R. Behr in "Edges and vertices in a unique signed circle in a signed graph" (arXiv:1610.02107; published in AKCE Int. J. Graphs Comb., 2017). Behr characterizes when an edge lies in a unique signed (negative or positive) circle in terms of bridges of a circle and the 2-separation/Tutte decomposition structure of the underlying graph, together with sign conditions on the pieces.

status_evidence.title: Edges and Vertices in a Unique Signed Circle in a Signed Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Behr examines conditions under which a signed graph contains an edge or vertex contained in a unique negative or positive circle; the underlying graph structure is characterized in terms of bridges of a circle.
status_evidence.claim: Behr provides a structural characterization of edges lying in a unique negative (or positive) circle of a signed graph.

status_evidence.title: Edges and vertices in a unique signed circle in a signed graph - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Published version characterizing the underlying graph structure necessary, in terms of bridges and 2-separations, for an edge to belong to a unique signed circle.
status_evidence.claim: Published solution to the unique-negative-circle-through-an-edge problem.
